common_name: Brother Cadfael Rose (Large Deep Pink Fragrant David Austin Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Brother Cadfael bears some of the largest flowers in the David Austin English rose line, on a vigorous, sturdy shrub.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost. Introduced by David Austin in 1990 and named for the fictional medieval monk-detective, Brother Cadfael produces exceptionally large, deeply cupped, rich rose-pink double blooms with a strong, classic old-rose fragrance, among the biggest individual flowers found in the English rose line. Its sturdy, well-branched shrub supports the heavy flower heads without excessive flopping, and it reblooms in flushes from late spring through fall. Prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and deadhead spent blooms through the season to sustain repeat flowering.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive

common_name: Desdemona Rose (Blush-White Fragrant David Austin Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Desdemona bears blush-white, seashell-shaped blooms that open from soft pink buds, a more recent David Austin introduction bred for good disease resistance.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost. Desdemona, a modern David Austin introduction, bears elegant, seashell-shaped blooms opening from soft pink buds to a delicate blush-white, with a strong myrrh fragrance, on a well-branched, disease-resistant shrub bred with the improved health that has become a hallmark of more recent Austin rose introductions. It reblooms in generous flushes from late spring through fall. Prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and deadhead spent blooms through the season to sustain continued flowering.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive

common_name: The Poet's Wife Rose (Rich Yellow Fragrant David Austin Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; The Poet's Wife is a modern David Austin introduction bred with strong disease resistance and a rich, fruity fragrance.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost. The Poet's Wife bears rich, deep yellow, cupped double blooms with a strong, fruity fragrance, one of the more saturated yellow tones in the modern David Austin English rose line, opening on a compact, well-branched, disease-resistant shrub. It reblooms generously from late spring through fall, and its clear yellow color pairs well with blues, purples, and whites in a mixed border. Prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and deadhead spent blooms through the season to sustain continued flowering.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive

common_name: Bathsheba Rose (Apricot-Pink Climbing David Austin Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation and a support if trained as a climber; Bathsheba can be grown as a large shrub or trained on a fence, pillar, or arbor.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost, providing a trellis, pillar, or fence if training as a climber. Bathsheba, a modern David Austin climbing rose, bears large, richly petaled, rosette-shaped blooms in a warm blend of apricot and soft pink with a strong old-rose fragrance, opening on long, vigorous canes that make it well suited to a large arbor, pergola, or wall. It reblooms in strong flushes from late spring through fall. Prune to control size and shape in late winter — thinning old wood if trained as a climber, or cutting canes back by a third if grown as a large shrub — and provide good air circulation to keep foliage clean through the growing season.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive
